Degrade-not-block keeps BD22: the worst case is the duplicate the fold already skips. Per-log dedupe cannot move a home: registeredAt reads a log's FIRST start, so record-integrity D9 is unaffected.

- 2026-09-15T16:09:22.982Z — chose **1.4 formatter defence in two levers: (1) init writes .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json in the shape the host's own formatter would produce — indent resolved biome.json(c) json.formatter > biome formatter > prettier config (JSON forms + package.json "prettier") > .editorconfig > 2 spaces, with primitive-only arrays collapsed onto one line when they fit (Prettier and Biome both do this; verified on biome 2.5.13 and prettier 3); (2) a new doctor axis "Formatter hazards" that names Biome, Prettier and markdownlint when their config is present and .sofar is not excluded, and --fix adds the exclusion the tool itself documents: Biome v2 `!**/.sofar` in files.includes (v1 `.sofar` in files.ignore, version read from $schema then node_modules), `.sofar/` in .prettierignore, `.sofar/` in .markdownlintignore or `**/.sofar/**` in a markdownlint-cli2 `ignores`. - 2026-09-15T16:25:53.038Z — chose **1.5 input forms: `sofar event append --payload` and `sofar remember [text]` each accept the JSON/text three ways — inline as today, `-` for stdin (the quoted-heredoc form the AGENTS block now shows: `--payload - <<'EOF' … EOF`), and `@<path>` for a file; with the value omitted and stdin piped, stdin is read. `remember --supersedes <M-handle>` records `supersedes` on memory_promoted as the QUALIFIED handle `<slug> M<n>` (a bare `M<n>` resolves against the target initiative; either form is validated to name an existing memory before the append). Supersession lets an outdated fact be replaced without a correction event that leaves doctor nagging for both.
- 2026-09-15T16:35:23.037Z — chose **1.6 drive diagnostics: the adapter exit record (SessionExit) carries `stderr_tail` (what the agent wrote to stderr, last chunk) and `spawn_error` (ENOENT and friends), both adapters fill them; the driver renders one `describeExit` line — exit code or signal, the spawn error, the last non-empty stderr line clipped — and puts it (a) on the progress line of every unresolved launch and every stall handoff, (b) in the run_stopped note for a stall stop (`last: …`), and (c) as an optional `detail` field on the stall/threshold handoff event so the cause is durable per session, not only in the driver's stderr. The handoff REASON is still read from the fold alone (D5) — detail annotates, never decides.** over (a) progress lines only — a detached run's stderr is not the record, and the next driver resumes from the record; (b) trusting the exit code or stderr to classify the handoff — D5 forbids it, and an agent that crashed after writing back still handed off on what the record shows; (c) appending a note_added per failed launch — record hygiene: a launch that registered no session files no handoff (D3), and a note would be a second event type saying the same thing. because Round 1's stalls read `no session registered … (exit 1)` and nothing else, so a missing binary, a logged-out agent and a crashed hook all looked identical and cost the operator a transcript hunt. The adapters already buffer the stderr tail and the spawn error for their own use; carrying them onto the exit record is the cheapest path to `every launch failure names its cause`.
- 2026-09-15T16:40:48.341Z — chose **2.1 four levers, each a separate ablation arm (D5): (A) the digest ends its decisions block with one line naming the NEXT handles — `Next ids: D<n+1>, M<m+1>` — so a session can cite the decision or memory it is about to log without a fold or a get_state; (B) sofar_update_task returns bare {ok, event_id} on every status — the standing-constraint echo on `active` (drift-hardening 4.1) is dropped, superseding that lever; the constraints stay injected at SessionStart and enforced mechanically by the point-of-use guard (§Hooks); (C) sofar_end_session takes `tasks?: [{task_id, status, note?}]`, validated as a whole before any append and applied in order under the session before session_ended, returning `tasks_applied`; (D) the MCP server declares `instructions` (SDK initialize) telling a client with deferred tools to load the core five in ONE ToolSearch and to skip get_state after the hook injection; the CLAUDE.md block's DURING/BEFORE FINISHING lines say task changes may ride the write-back.** over (a) keeping the constraint echo but capping it — every echo repeats text the session already holds from SessionStart, and the guard hook is the enforcing half, so a capped echo is still pure repetition; (b) a separate sofar_batch tool — one more schema on every turn (2.4 is trimming the surface); (c) putting the next ids in tool responses only — the digest is read before the first write, which is when a session plans its citations; (d) instructions long enough to restate the protocol — the block already does, and instructions ride every initialize. because Round 1 measured sofar's share of tool calls at 32–38% per session: one update_task per status change (2–4 per task), a get_state or find to learn the next D id before citing it, a ToolSearch per deferred tool, and constraint echoes of ~600 chars per activation. Each lever removes one of those call classes without removing any information a session needs, so the prediction (share ≤20%, −3 to −5 turns per session) is attributable arm by arm.

Nothing moves to UserPromptSubmit: the per-prompt path already carries the drift nudge and the landed line, and the shipping check is two git spawns that D6 keeps off that path. Supersedes placement only — every line keeps its wording and budget: BD43 (Session line near the top), record-integrity 4.1 (Git above Goal), session-orientation 2.2 (recent-work line leads), felt-cost 2.2 (advisory precedes the block), record-index 3.3 (adjacency last in the current block), commit-attribution 3.2 (shipping notice composed around the block). Byte-stability (felt-cost 1.2) is restated precisely: for identical state and options-minus-notices, the block is byte-identical up to the notices. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): cache-creation tokens per session −15%; local proxy = the share of the block that is byte-identical between consecutive sessions of the same record, 0.8% before (182 pairs, every one diverging at line 3).** over (a) moving the Session id out of the block into a separate hook line after it — the same bytes at the same position, one more surface to teach; (b) leaving the notices as a preface and only reordering the block — the shipping notice renders on every session of an unpushed branch and is the first byte, so the reorder would buy nothing here; (c) sending staleness, notes and the read-back through UserPromptSubmit instead — they are state-derived and cost nothing, and the per-prompt path is budgeted at 100ms (D6); (d) dropping the Session line from the digest and relying on hook-registered adoption — start_session needs the id in the agent's hands, and 1.1 just put it on the unbound notice for the same reason. because Measured on this repo's records: of 182 consecutive-session pairs, the digest shares 0.8% of its bytes — the title only — because the per-session `Session:` line is line 3 and the `Git:` sha is line 5, ahead of a goal, four verbatim rules, 1,500 chars of repo memory and the phase list that do not change between sessions. Prompt caching matches prefixes, so bytes that never change belong before bytes that change every session; the gain is only realized when the host's own prefix (system prompt, CLAUDE.md, its git status) is also identical — same-sha restarts, parallel sessions, compaction re-fires — which is the honest bound on the prediction and why the local proxy measures the block alone.
